title: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing
name: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing
metaTitle: NNN and STNL Property Sourcing in Phoenix, AZ
metaDescription: Sourcing net lease and single-tenant retail pads along Phoenix growth corridors for 1031 exchange investors who want passive replacement property.

sections.html: Single-tenant net lease is the low-maintenance play a lot of exchangers want after selling something that took real management time. Phoenix has plenty of it, but the good pads go quick once a corridor gets hot.

sections.heading: Where the Pads Get Built
sections.html: New single-tenant retail pads keep landing along Bell Road, Baseline Road, and the arterials feeding new rooftops in the West Valley. Quick-service restaurants, pharmacies, and dollar-store formats follow the same population growth pushing new apartments into Goodyear and Surprise. Existing pads in older corridors like Camelback and Central trade less often but come with longer operating history to underwrite.

sections.heading: Reading the Tenant Behind the Lease
sections.html:
Corporate-guaranteed leases from national tenants price tighter than a franchisee-guaranteed lease, even on an identical building. We pull the guarantor structure before you see a listing, because a franchisee with three locations carries different risk than the same building leased to the parent company.

Lease term remaining matters as much as the tenant name. A strong tenant with three years left on the lease is a different investment than the same tenant with fifteen years left.

sections.heading: Screening a Net Lease Candidate
sections.html:
We run every net lease pad through the same short checklist before it makes your list:

  • Guarantor type: corporate, franchisee, or personal
  • Remaining primary lease term and renewal options
  • Rent escalations built into the lease
  • Traffic counts and access at the specific corner
  • Competing pads permitted or under construction nearby

That's enough to separate a durable income stream from a pad that looks fine until the lease comes up for renewal.

sections.heading: Fitting Net Lease Into a Tight Identification Window
sections.html:
Net lease deals close faster than most commercial property because there's no operating business to underwrite, which makes them a common fit when an exchanger is short on time inside the 45-day identification window. We keep a rotating list of vetted pads so you're identifying real, priced deals instead of guessing at value.

We don't calculate boot or advise on tax treatment. If the pad you're eyeing carries less debt or a lower price than what you sold, have your CPA check that before you finalize the identification.

sections.heading: Why Net Lease Cap Rates Move Corridor by Corridor
sections.html:
A pad on Bell Road with heavy traffic counts and a corporate-guaranteed tenant prices tighter than the same tenant on a slower arterial in an older corridor. That gap reflects more than the tenant name; it also reflects how much competing retail is planned nearby and how the surrounding rooftops are trending. We compare cap rates within the same corridor rather than against a metro-wide average, since a Camelback pad and a Buckeye pad aren't really the same market.

Land cost also plays into new pad pricing on the growth corridors. Ground leases and build-to-suit pads in Goodyear or Surprise sometimes carry a premium tied to how scarce corner lots have gotten as those cities fill in, which is worth knowing before you compare a new pad's cap rate to an older corridor's.

sections.heading: The Trap With This Asset Class
sections.html:
The biggest mistake we see is buying purely for the tenant name and skipping the lease abstract. A great tenant with a weak lease, thin escalations, or an early termination option can underperform a lesser-known tenant with a clean long-term lease. We read the actual lease before recommending anything.

A second trap is assuming a pad's traffic counts will hold steady. Road widening projects and new signal timing along growth corridors can change access to a corner overnight, so we check any planned roadwork near a candidate pad before it goes on your list.

sections.heading: Ground Lease Versus Fee Simple Ownership
sections.html: Some net lease pads sell as fee simple ownership of land and building, while others sell as a ground lease position where the tenant owns the building and you own the underlying land. The two structures price differently and carry different risk, since a ground lease investor never deals with building maintenance but also has less control if the tenant vacates. We confirm which structure a listing actually is before you assume a cap rate comparison is apples to apples.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a corporate-guaranteed and franchisee-guaranteed net lease?
faqs.a: A corporate guarantee ties the lease obligation to the parent company's balance sheet, while a franchisee guarantee ties it to a smaller operator, sometimes just one or two locations. We flag which one you're getting before you commit.

faqs.q: Why do net lease deals fit well inside a short identification window?
faqs.a: There's no business operation to underwrite, just a building, a tenant, and a lease, so due diligence and closing move faster than most other commercial property. That timeline benefit doesn't change the tax rules, so still confirm dates with your qualified intermediary.

faqs.q: Which Phoenix corridors have the most new net lease pad development?
faqs.a: Bell Road and Baseline Road, plus the arterials feeding new rooftops in Goodyear and Surprise, have seen the most recent pad construction tied to population growth in those submarkets.

faqs.q: What lease terms matter most when comparing two similar net lease buildings?
faqs.a: Remaining primary term, renewal options, and built-in rent escalations. Two buildings with the same tenant name can have very different lease economics underneath.

faqs.q: Can a net lease property with a short remaining lease term still work as a 1031 replacement?
faqs.a: It can, but the pricing and financing usually reflect that risk. We show you the real remaining term before you identify the property so there are no surprises at closing.
